dialogue.text: This is the story of how George Orwell wrote Animal Farm, the mountain he had to climb to get it published, and the enormous personal tragedy that ran beneath.
dialogue.zh: 這是喬治·奧威爾如何寫出《動物農場》的故事，他為了出版這本書所要攀登的高山，以及背後巨大的個人悲劇。
dialogue.ja: これはジョージ・オーウェルが『動物農場』を書き上げるまでの物語であり、出版までの困難な道のりと、その背後にあった大きな個人的悲劇についてです。
dialogue.local: This is the story of how George Orwell wrote Animal Farm, the mountain he had to climb to get it published, and the enormous personal tragedy that ran beneath.
dialogue.en: This is the story of how George Orwell wrote Animal Farm, the mountain he had to climb to get it published, and the enormous personal tragedy that ran beneath.

dialogue.text: All he said that he got the idea for Animal Farm as long ago as 1937, presumably the rose out of his Spanish experiences fighting against Franco.
dialogue.zh: 他說他早在1937年就有了《動物農場》的構想，這大概是源自他在西班牙反抗佛朗哥的經歷。
dialogue.ja: 彼は『動物農場』のアイデアを1937年にはすでに思いついていたと言っており、それはおそらくスペイン内戦でフランコに対抗した経験から生まれたものです。
dialogue.local: All he said that he got the idea for Animal Farm as long ago as 1937, presumably the rose out of his Spanish experiences fighting against Franco.
dialogue.en: All he said that he got the idea for Animal Farm as long ago as 1937, presumably the rose out of his Spanish experiences fighting against Franco.

dialogue.text: Although it's purportedly a fable written for a juvenile audience, Animal Farm is always going to be controversial.
dialogue.zh: 雖然《動物農場》表面上是寫給青少年的寓言，但它始終會引起爭議。
dialogue.ja: 表向きは若い読者向けの寓話とされていますが、『動物農場』は常に議論を呼ぶ作品です。
dialogue.local: Although it's purportedly a fable written for a juvenile audience, Animal Farm is always going to be controversial.
dialogue.en: Although it's purportedly a fable written for a juvenile audience, Animal Farm is always going to be controversial.

dialogue.text: Essentially, it's a satire of the Soviet Revolution, done in forensic detail at each major event in the progress of the Soviet Revolution as its answer in call in Animal Farm, and all well knew even as he began that this was going to make trouble, and so there's a letter to his friend, the Russian academic, globe-strew from February, 1944, where he says,
dialogue.zh: 本質上，它是對蘇聯革命的諷刺，對蘇聯革命進程中的每個重大事件都進行了細緻的描寫。奧威爾從一開始就知道這會引起麻煩，因此他在1944年2月寫信給他的俄國學者朋友格洛布斯特魯說，
dialogue.ja: 本質的にはソビエト革命を風刺した作品であり、革命の主要な出来事を詳細に描いています。オーウェルはこれが問題を引き起こすことを最初から理解しており、1944年2月にロシアの学者グローブストルーに宛てた手紙でこう述べています。
dialogue.local: Essentially, it's a satire of the Soviet Revolution, done in forensic detail at each major event in the progress of the Soviet Revolution as its answer in call in Animal Farm, and all well knew even as he began that this was going to make trouble, and so there's a letter to his friend, the Russian academic, globe-strew from February, 1944, where he says,
dialogue.en: Essentially, it's a satire of the Soviet Revolution, done in forensic detail at each major event in the progress of the Soviet Revolution as its answer in call in Animal Farm, and all well knew even as he began that this was going to make trouble, and so there's a letter to his friend, the Russian academic, globe-strew from February, 1944, where he says,

dialogue.text: I'm writing a little squib, which might amuse you when it comes out, but it is so not okay politically that I don't feel certain in advance that anyone will publish it, perhaps that gives you a hint of its subject.
dialogue.zh: 我正在寫一個小短文，出版時可能會讓你覺得有趣，但政治上非常敏感，我不確定會有人願意出版它，也許這能讓你猜到它的主題。
dialogue.ja: 今、小さな短編を書いているんだ。出版されたら君を楽しませるかもしれないけど、政治的には非常に問題があるから、誰かが出版してくれるかどうかはわからない。これで内容のヒントになるかもしれないね。
dialogue.local: I'm writing a little squib, which might amuse you when it comes out, but it is so not okay politically that I don't feel certain in advance that anyone will publish it, perhaps that gives you a hint of its subject.
dialogue.en: I'm writing a little squib, which might amuse you when it comes out, but it is so not okay politically that I don't feel certain in advance that anyone will publish it, perhaps that gives you a hint of its subject.

dialogue.text: That was written on the 17th of February, and so by the middle of the next month when Orwell is writing to Gellance, Victor Gellance, who published his first four novels in England, and Gellance, although by this point was probably not a paid-up style in this, in the thirties, he'd certainly taken some of his orders from King Street, the headquarters of the British Communist Party, and Orwell writes to him, dear Mr. Gellance quite matter of fact, I mean, all I'll always grab the ball by the horns on these occasions, I think this comes under the heading of fiction, it's a little fairy story, but I must tell you that it is, I think, completely unacceptable politically from your point of view, it is an anti-stylin.
dialogue.zh: 這封信寫於2月17日，到下個月中，奧威爾寫信給維克多·蓋蘭斯，他在英國出版了奧威爾的前四部小說。蓋蘭斯雖然在30年代可能不再是正式黨員，但他確實接受過英國共產黨總部金街的指示。奧威爾寫信給他說：「親愛的蓋蘭斯先生，說實話，我總是直面問題，我認為這屬於小說範疇，是個小童話，但我必須告訴你，從你的政治立場來看，這是完全不能接受的，這是反共的。」
dialogue.ja: これは2月17日に書かれたもので、翌月中旬にはオーウェルがヴィクター・ゲランスに手紙を書いています。ゲランスはイギリスで彼の最初の4冊の小説を出版しましたが、30年代には共産党の正式なメンバーではなかったかもしれませんが、確かに英国共産党本部のキングストリートから指示を受けていました。オーウェルは彼にこう書いています。「親愛なるゲランスさん、率直に言って、こういう時はいつも問題に正面から取り組みますが、これはフィクションの範疇に入ると思います。小さな童話ですが、あなたの政治的立場からすると完全に受け入れられないと思います。これは反共的です。」
dialogue.local: That was written on the 17th of February, and so by the middle of the next month when Orwell is writing to Gellance, Victor Gellance, who published his first four novels in England, and Gellance, although by this point was probably not a paid-up style in this, in the thirties, he'd certainly taken some of his orders from King Street, the headquarters of the British Communist Party, and Orwell writes to him, dear Mr. Gellance quite matter of fact, I mean, all I'll always grab the ball by the horns on these occasions, I think this comes under the heading of fiction, it's a little fairy story, but I must tell you that it is, I think, completely unacceptable politically from your point of view, it is an anti-stylin.
dialogue.en: That was written on the 17th of February, and so by the middle of the next month when Orwell is writing to Gellance, Victor Gellance, who published his first four novels in England, and Gellance, although by this point was probably not a paid-up style in this, in the thirties, he'd certainly taken some of his orders from King Street, the headquarters of the British Communist Party, and Orwell writes to him, dear Mr. Gellance quite matter of fact, I mean, all I'll always grab the ball by the horns on these occasions, I think this comes under the heading of fiction, it's a little fairy story, but I must tell you that it is, I think, completely unacceptable politically from your point of view, it is an anti-stylin.

dialogue.text: So he was effectively telling Gellance that he wasn't going to want to publish it, which is the effect is what happened.
dialogue.zh: 所以他實際上是在告訴蓋蘭斯，他不會想要出版這本書，結果也確實如此。
dialogue.ja: つまり、彼はゲランスに対して、この本を出版したくないだろうと伝えていたわけで、実際にそうなりました。
dialogue.local: So he was effectively telling Gellance that he wasn't going to want to publish it, which is the effect is what happened.
dialogue.en: So he was effectively telling Gellance that he wasn't going to want to publish it, which is the effect is what happened.

dialogue.text: The fellow Nicholson and Watson turned it down, certainly on the grounds that why should we be offending one of our greatest political allies that are such a crucial juncture in the Second World War?
dialogue.zh: 尼科爾森和沃森出版社拒絕了，理由當然是：在第二次世界大戰這個關鍵時刻，我們為何要冒犯我們最重要的政治盟友之一？
dialogue.ja: ニコルソン＆ワトソン社はこれを拒否しました。理由は、第二次世界大戦の重要な局面で、なぜ我々の最大の政治的同盟国の一つを怒らせる必要があるのか、というものでした。
dialogue.local: The fellow Nicholson and Watson turned it down, certainly on the grounds that why should we be offending one of our greatest political allies that are such a crucial juncture in the Second World War?
dialogue.en: The fellow Nicholson and Watson turned it down, certainly on the grounds that why should we be offending one of our greatest political allies that are such a crucial juncture in the Second World War?

dialogue.text: T.S. Eliot, a favour and favour, turned it down, more or less on those grounds, but also adding what might to a modern era seem to rather block the marks about the nature of the pigs.
dialogue.zh: T.S.艾略特也拒絕了，理由大致相同，但他還補充了一些在現代看來可能顯得有些奇怪的關於豬的性質的看法。
dialogue.ja: T.S.エリオットもほぼ同じ理由でこれを拒否しましたが、現代の視点から見るとやや偏った、豚の性質に関する意見も付け加えました。
dialogue.local: T.S. Eliot, a favour and favour, turned it down, more or less on those grounds, but also adding what might to a modern era seem to rather block the marks about the nature of the pigs.
dialogue.en: T.S. Eliot, a favour and favour, turned it down, more or less on those grounds, but also adding what might to a modern era seem to rather block the marks about the nature of the pigs.

dialogue.text: And so Eliot writes in, this is July 1944, so the process has been going on for four months by then.
dialogue.zh: 於是艾略特在1944年7月寫道，當時這個過程已經持續了四個月。
dialogue.ja: そしてエリオットは1944年7月にこう書いています。この時点で出版の過程はすでに4ヶ月続いていました。
dialogue.local: And so Eliot writes in, this is July 1944, so the process has been going on for four months by then.
dialogue.en: And so Eliot writes in, this is July 1944, so the process has been going on for four months by then.

dialogue.text: And he says, after all, your pigs are far more intelligent than the other animals, and therefore the best qualified to run the farm, in fact, they couldn't have been an animal farmer tall without them, so what was needed, someone might argue, was not more communism, but the more public spirited pigs.
dialogue.zh: 他說，畢竟，你的豬比其他動物聰明得多，因此最適合管理農場，事實上，沒有它們，這本《動物農場》根本無法成書。有人可能會說，所需要的不是更多的共產主義，而是更有公共精神的豬。
dialogue.ja: 彼はこう述べています。結局のところ、あなたの描く豚は他の動物よりもはるかに賢く、農場を運営するのに最も適任です。実際、彼らなしでは『動物農場』は成り立たなかったでしょう。必要なのは、より多くの共産主義ではなく、より公共心のある豚たちだと主張する人もいるでしょう。
dialogue.local: And he says, after all, your pigs are far more intelligent than the other animals, and therefore the best qualified to run the farm, in fact, they couldn't have been an animal farmer tall without them, so what was needed, someone might argue, was not more communism, but the more public spirited pigs.
dialogue.en: And he says, after all, your pigs are far more intelligent than the other animals, and therefore the best qualified to run the farm, in fact, they couldn't have been an animal farmer tall without them, so what was needed, someone might argue, was not more communism, but the more public spirited pigs.

dialogue.text: So that was Eliot's reason for turning it down.
dialogue.zh: 這就是艾略特拒絕的理由。
dialogue.ja: これがエリオットが拒否した理由です。
dialogue.local: So that was Eliot's reason for turning it down.
dialogue.en: So that was Eliot's reason for turning it down.

dialogue.text: More sinister, even than this, probably, was the reason for which one of them ate them and ate themselves was very keen on publishing the book, but then advised by an official at the Ministry of Information, man called Peter Smollett, subsequently revealed as a communist spy that the book would be very unhelpful in the current political situation,
dialogue.zh: 甚至比這更險惡的原因是，其中一位非常熱衷於出版這本書，但後來受到情報部一名官員彼得·斯莫萊特的建議（他後來被揭露為共產黨間諜），認為這本書在當前政治形勢下非常不利，
dialogue.ja: さらに悪質だったのは、ある出版社がこの本の出版に非常に熱心だったものの、情報省の職員ピーター・スモレット（後に共産党のスパイと判明）から、現在の政治状況ではこの本は非常に不都合だと助言されたことです。
dialogue.local: More sinister, even than this, probably, was the reason for which one of them ate them and ate themselves was very keen on publishing the book, but then advised by an official at the Ministry of Information, man called Peter Smollett, subsequently revealed as a communist spy that the book would be very unhelpful in the current political situation,
dialogue.en: More sinister, even than this, probably, was the reason for which one of them ate them and ate themselves was very keen on publishing the book, but then advised by an official at the Ministry of Information, man called Peter Smollett, subsequently revealed as a communist spy that the book would be very unhelpful in the current political situation,

dialogue.text: so it was a very, very close run thing until finally, Secretary Norberg, who published his Spanish book, Thomas de Catalonia, agreed to publish it in the summer of 1944.
dialogue.zh: 所以這件事非常驚險，直到1944年夏天，出版了他的西班牙書《加泰隆尼亞的托馬斯》的諾伯格秘書才同意出版它。
dialogue.ja: そのため非常にギリギリの状況でしたが、最終的にスペインに関する本『トーマス・デ・カタロニア』を出版したノルバーグ書記が1944年夏に出版に同意しました。
dialogue.local: so it was a very, very close run thing until finally, Secretary Norberg, who published his Spanish book, Thomas de Catalonia, agreed to publish it in the summer of 1944.
dialogue.en: so it was a very, very close run thing until finally, Secretary Norberg, who published his Spanish book, Thomas de Catalonia, agreed to publish it in the summer of 1944.

dialogue.text: It doesn't find me come out until August 1945, almost as the war is over, well, of course, it became an enormous success, or whilst most successful book he'd so far published, fan letters from the great and good.
dialogue.zh: 直到1945年8月，也就是戰爭快結束時才出版，當然，它成為了巨大的成功，是他迄今為止最成功的書，收到了許多名流的粉絲信。
dialogue.ja: 1945年8月、ほぼ戦争が終わる頃にようやく出版されました。もちろん、それは大成功を収め、彼がこれまでに出版した中で最も成功した本となり、多くの著名人からファンレターが届きました。
dialogue.local: It doesn't find me come out until August 1945, almost as the war is over, well, of course, it became an enormous success, or whilst most successful book he'd so far published, fan letters from the great and good.
dialogue.en: It doesn't find me come out until August 1945, almost as the war is over, well, of course, it became an enormous success, or whilst most successful book he'd so far published, fan letters from the great and good.

dialogue.text: There's a wonderful story of the Queen, Queen Elizabeth, George VI, wife who was very bookish in her way, sending out for a copy and discovering all the West End book shots hadn't got it.
dialogue.zh: 有一個很棒的故事，說英國女王伊麗莎白（喬治六世的妻子）非常愛書，派人去買一本，結果發現西區的所有書店都沒有存貨。
dialogue.ja: 素敵な話があります。ジョージ6世の妻であるエリザベス女王は非常に読書好きで、コピーを取り寄せようとしましたが、ウェストエンドの書店にはどこにも在庫がありませんでした。
dialogue.local: There's a wonderful story of the Queen, Queen Elizabeth, George VI, wife who was very bookish in her way, sending out for a copy and discovering all the West End book shots hadn't got it.
dialogue.en: There's a wonderful story of the Queen, Queen Elizabeth, George VI, wife who was very bookish in her way, sending out for a copy and discovering all the West End book shots hadn't got it.

dialogue.text: And the emissary, I believe, actually in the Royal Code, she had to go to Orwell's and George Woodcock's anarchist bookshop and buy a copy there.
dialogue.zh: 我相信女王派出的使者，實際上是按照皇室規定，必須去奧威爾和喬治·伍德科克的無政府主義書店買一本。
dialogue.ja: そして使者は、王室の規則に従って、オーウェルとジョージ・ウッドコックのアナーキスト書店に行ってコピーを購入しなければなりませんでした。
dialogue.local: And the emissary, I believe, actually in the Royal Code, she had to go to Orwell's and George Woodcock's anarchist bookshop and buy a copy there.
dialogue.en: And the emissary, I believe, actually in the Royal Code, she had to go to Orwell's and George Woodcock's anarchist bookshop and buy a copy there.

dialogue.text: So that's a wonderful sort of the meeting of two worlds in the publication of Animal Farm.
dialogue.zh: 這真是一個奇妙的兩個世界在《動物農場》出版時的交會。
dialogue.ja: これは『動物農場』の出版における二つの世界の素晴らしい出会いと言えるでしょう。
dialogue.local: So that's a wonderful sort of the meeting of two worlds in the publication of Animal Farm.
dialogue.en: So that's a wonderful sort of the meeting of two worlds in the publication of Animal Farm.

dialogue.text: It was taken out by the book clubs in America, sold hundreds of thousands of copies there, but also did well here, the first, or first popular success, the first book that he actually made very much money out of in the dozen years that he'd been publishing prior to that.
dialogue.zh: 它被美國的讀書會採用，銷售了數十萬冊，在這裡也賣得很好，是他出版十二年來第一本真正賺大錢的暢銷書。
dialogue.ja: アメリカの読書クラブで取り上げられ、数十万部売れました。ここでも成功し、彼が出版してから12年間で初めて大きな収益を上げた本となりました。
dialogue.local: It was taken out by the book clubs in America, sold hundreds of thousands of copies there, but also did well here, the first, or first popular success, the first book that he actually made very much money out of in the dozen years that he'd been publishing prior to that.
dialogue.en: It was taken out by the book clubs in America, sold hundreds of thousands of copies there, but also did well here, the first, or first popular success, the first book that he actually made very much money out of in the dozen years that he'd been publishing prior to that.

dialogue.text: The writing and the submission and the process of publication of Animal Farm happened at exactly the same time as a series of crises in Orwell's personal life.
dialogue.zh: 《動物農場》的寫作、投稿和出版過程，正好與奧威爾個人生活中的一連串危機同時發生。
dialogue.ja: 『動物農場』の執筆、投稿、出版の過程は、ちょうどオーウェルの私生活における一連の危機と重なっていました。
dialogue.local: The writing and the submission and the process of publication of Animal Farm happened at exactly the same time as a series of crises in Orwell's personal life.
dialogue.en: The writing and the submission and the process of publication of Animal Farm happened at exactly the same time as a series of crises in Orwell's personal life.

dialogue.text: By this point, he'd been married to his first wife, Eileen, for over seven years. They couldn't conceive a child.
dialogue.zh: 此時，他已與第一任妻子艾琳結婚超過七年，但他們無法懷孕生子。
dialogue.ja: この時点で彼は最初の妻アイリーンと7年以上結婚していましたが、子供を授かることができませんでした。
dialogue.local: By this point, he'd been married to his first wife, Eileen, for over seven years. They couldn't conceive a child.
dialogue.en: By this point, he'd been married to his first wife, Eileen, for over seven years. They couldn't conceive a child.

dialogue.text: Well, Orwell always fancied himself sterile, but Eileen had my problems of her own.
dialogue.zh: 奧威爾一直認為自己不育，但艾琳也有自己的問題。
dialogue.ja: オーウェルは自分が不妊だと思っていましたが、アイリーンにも彼女自身の問題がありました。
dialogue.local: Well, Orwell always fancied himself sterile, but Eileen had my problems of her own.
dialogue.en: Well, Orwell always fancied himself sterile, but Eileen had my problems of her own.

dialogue.text: By this point, they decided to adopt a process that would be facilitated by Eileen's sister-in-law, who's a GP and had access to these kind of procedures.
dialogue.zh: 於是他們決定採用收養的方式，這由艾琳的嫂子協助，她是一名全科醫生，能夠接觸這類程序。
dialogue.ja: そこで彼らは養子縁組を決めました。これはアイリーンの義理の姉が一般開業医であり、このような手続きを手助けできたからです。
dialogue.local: By this point, they decided to adopt a process that would be facilitated by Eileen's sister-in-law, who's a GP and had access to these kind of procedures.
dialogue.en: By this point, they decided to adopt a process that would be facilitated by Eileen's sister-in-law, who's a GP and had access to these kind of procedures.

dialogue.text: And so in the early summer of 1944, just as all of the publishing crises are going on, they adopt a small boy named Richard Horatio Blair, but this too was fraught with difficulty because it almost precisely at the same time, the little masonette they were living in London, NW6, bombed out, they're effectively homeless,
dialogue.zh: 於是1944年初夏，正值出版危機時期，他們收養了一個名叫理查德·霍雷肖·布萊爾的小男孩，但同時他們在倫敦NW6居住的小公寓被炸毀，他們幾乎無家可歸，
dialogue.ja: そして1944年初夏、出版の危機が続く中、彼らはリチャード・ホレイショ・ブレアという小さな男の子を養子にしました。しかしほぼ同時に、彼らがロンドンNW6に住んでいた小さなメゾネットが爆撃され、事実上ホームレスになってしまいました。
dialogue.local: And so in the early summer of 1944, just as all of the publishing crises are going on, they adopt a small boy named Richard Horatio Blair, but this too was fraught with difficulty because it almost precisely at the same time, the little masonette they were living in London, NW6, bombed out, they're effectively homeless,
dialogue.en: And so in the early summer of 1944, just as all of the publishing crises are going on, they adopt a small boy named Richard Horatio Blair, but this too was fraught with difficulty because it almost precisely at the same time, the little masonette they were living in London, NW6, bombed out, they're effectively homeless,

dialogue.text: but it got worse in the spring of 1945, infinitely infinitely worse, because Orwell went off at the instigation of David Asper and the observer, went off to what was the now-occupied Europe as a war correspondent, Fender Spatch's back, the Sunday newspaper.
dialogue.zh: 但情況在1945年春天變得更糟，無比糟糕，因為奧威爾在大衛·阿斯珀和《觀察家報》的促使下，作為戰地記者前往當時被佔領的歐洲，為《星期日報》報導。
dialogue.ja: しかし1945年春には状況がさらに悪化しました。デイビッド・アスパーと『オブザーバー』の働きかけで、オーウェルは戦争特派員として占領下のヨーロッパへ向かい、『サンデー・ニューズペーパー』に記事を書きました。
dialogue.local: but it got worse in the spring of 1945, infinitely infinitely worse, because Orwell went off at the instigation of David Asper and the observer, went off to what was the now-occupied Europe as a war correspondent, Fender Spatch's back, the Sunday newspaper.
dialogue.en: but it got worse in the spring of 1945, infinitely infinitely worse, because Orwell went off at the instigation of David Asper and the observer, went off to what was the now-occupied Europe as a war correspondent, Fender Spatch's back, the Sunday newspaper.

dialogue.text: Eileen went into hospital in Newcastle, near Newcastle, but a supposedly routine operation on fibroids in the womb, Hart gave out on the operating table, didn't come round, dive, and so Orwell was left a widower with a small child that he was resolved and determined to raise itself, and under the prospect of a book still aging very, very slowly towards publications.
dialogue.zh: 艾琳住進了紐卡斯爾附近的醫院，原本是子宮肌瘤的例行手術，但她在手術台上心臟停止，沒有醒來，去世了。於是奧威爾成了寡夫，帶著一個小孩，他決心親自撫養，並且面對著一本仍在緩慢出版的書。
dialogue.ja: アイリーンはニューカッスル近郊の病院に入院しました。子宮の筋腫のための通常の手術でしたが、手術中に心臓が止まり、意識を取り戻すことなく亡くなりました。こうしてオーウェルは未亡人となり、小さな子供を育てる決意を固めました。そして出版が非常に遅れている本のことも抱えていました。
dialogue.local: Eileen went into hospital in Newcastle, near Newcastle, but a supposedly routine operation on fibroids in the womb, Hart gave out on the operating table, didn't come round, dive, and so Orwell was left a widower with a small child that he was resolved and determined to raise itself, and under the prospect of a book still aging very, very slowly towards publications.
dialogue.en: Eileen went into hospital in Newcastle, near Newcastle, but a supposedly routine operation on fibroids in the womb, Hart gave out on the operating table, didn't come round, dive, and so Orwell was left a widower with a small child that he was resolved and determined to raise itself, and under the prospect of a book still aging very, very slowly towards publications.

dialogue.text: So the two great crises of Orwell's life, the professional and the personal, running together in the spring 1945, and he remained traumatised by that for some time.
dialogue.zh: 因此，奧威爾生命中兩大危機——職業和個人——在1945年春天同時發生，他因此受到長時間的創傷。
dialogue.ja: こうしてオーウェルの人生における二つの大きな危機、職業的なものと私生活のものが1945年春に重なり、彼はしばらくの間トラウマを抱え続けました。
dialogue.local: So the two great crises of Orwell's life, the professional and the personal, running together in the spring 1945, and he remained traumatised by that for some time.
dialogue.en: So the two great crises of Orwell's life, the professional and the personal, running together in the spring 1945, and he remained traumatised by that for some time.

dialogue.text: The answer to your first question, did I have any, did he give me anything of my mother? I have no recollection that he ever did.
dialogue.zh: 回答你的第一個問題，他有沒有給我任何關於我母親的東西？我不記得他有。
dialogue.ja: あなたの最初の質問に答えると、彼は私に母について何かを与えたことがあったか？私はその記憶がありません。
dialogue.local: The answer to your first question, did I have any, did he give me anything of my mother? I have no recollection that he ever did.
dialogue.en: The answer to your first question, did I have any, did he give me anything of my mother? I have no recollection that he ever did.

dialogue.text: Brothers was a different world. He was looking forward rather than backwards, I think.
dialogue.zh: 兄弟們的世界不同。我想他是向前看，而不是回頭看。
dialogue.ja: 兄弟たちは別の世界にいました。彼は過去ではなく未来を見ていたと思います。
dialogue.local: Brothers was a different world. He was looking forward rather than backwards, I think.
dialogue.en: Brothers was a different world. He was looking forward rather than backwards, I think.

dialogue.text: He certainly is hurt, was far deeper than he ever said to anybody.
dialogue.zh: 他確實受過傷，這傷痛比他對任何人說的都要深得多。
dialogue.ja: 彼は確かに傷ついていましたが、その痛みは誰にも言わなかったよりもはるかに深かったのです。
dialogue.local: He certainly is hurt, was far deeper than he ever said to anybody.
dialogue.en: He certainly is hurt, was far deeper than he ever said to anybody.

dialogue.text: Snowballs and himself to solve the problem of power on the farm.
dialogue.zh: 雪球和他自己解決了農場上的權力問題。
dialogue.ja: スノーボールと彼自身が農場の権力問題を解決しました。
dialogue.local: Snowballs and himself to solve the problem of power on the farm.
dialogue.en: Snowballs and himself to solve the problem of power on the farm.

dialogue.text: And so, didn't Napoleon.
dialogue.zh: 拿破崙也是如此。
dialogue.ja: そしてナポレオンも同様でした。
dialogue.local: And so, didn't Napoleon.
dialogue.en: And so, didn't Napoleon.

dialogue.text: All always said that he got the idea for animal farm by watching quite a small boy leading quite a big cart horse along a country road, and suddenly wondering what would happen if the roles were reversed and the cart horse decided that he didn't want to be led along the road by the small child.
dialogue.zh: 他總是說，他得到《動物農場》靈感是因為看到一個小男孩牽著一匹大馬走鄉間小路，突然想像如果角色互換，馬不想被小孩牽著會怎樣。
dialogue.ja: 彼はいつも、かなり小さな男の子が大きな荷馬車の馬を田舎道で引いているのを見て、『もし役割が逆になって、馬が小さな子供に引かれるのを嫌がったらどうなるだろう』と考えたことが『動物農場』のアイデアのきっかけだと言っていました。
dialogue.local: All always said that he got the idea for animal farm by watching quite a small boy leading quite a big cart horse along a country road, and suddenly wondering what would happen if the roles were reversed and the cart horse decided that he didn't want to be led along the road by the small child.
dialogue.en: All always said that he got the idea for animal farm by watching quite a small boy leading quite a big cart horse along a country road, and suddenly wondering what would happen if the roles were reversed and the cart horse decided that he didn't want to be led along the road by the small child.

dialogue.text: He was a great fan of allegory, allegory involving animals. I mean, there are swifty and resonances in animal farm.
dialogue.zh: 他非常喜歡寓言，尤其是涉及動物的寓言。我是說，《動物農場》中有斯威夫特的影響和共鳴。
dialogue.ja: 彼は寓話、特に動物を使った寓話の大ファンでした。『動物農場』にはスウィフトの影響や共鳴が見られます。
dialogue.local: He was a great fan of allegory, allegory involving animals. I mean, there are swifty and resonances in animal farm.
dialogue.en: He was a great fan of allegory, allegory involving animals. I mean, there are swifty and resonances in animal farm.

dialogue.text: He also liked the fables of the French writer Fontaine, but one or two critics have pointed out that the 1930s was the great age of the cartoon animal.
dialogue.zh: 他也喜歡法國作家方丹的寓言，但有評論指出1930年代是卡通動物的黃金時代。
dialogue.ja: 彼はフランスの作家フォントーヌの寓話も好みましたが、1930年代はカートゥーン動物の黄金時代だったと指摘する批評家もいます。
dialogue.local: He also liked the fables of the French writer Fontaine, but one or two critics have pointed out that the 1930s was the great age of the cartoon animal.
dialogue.en: He also liked the fables of the French writer Fontaine, but one or two critics have pointed out that the 1930s was the great age of the cartoon animal.

dialogue.text: The anthropomorphised creature who wandered around in Disney and other kinds of cartoons, and significantly, I think all well thought of a very early stage that would make a good cartoon.
dialogue.zh: 那些在迪士尼和其他卡通中出現的擬人化動物，奧威爾從很早期就認為這會是一個很好的卡通題材。
dialogue.ja: ディズニーやその他のカートゥーンに登場する擬人化された動物たちで、オーウェルは初期の段階からこれが良いカートゥーンになると考えていました。
dialogue.local: The anthropomorphised creature who wandered around in Disney and other kinds of cartoons, and significantly, I think all well thought of a very early stage that would make a good cartoon.
dialogue.en: The anthropomorphised creature who wandered around in Disney and other kinds of cartoons, and significantly, I think all well thought of a very early stage that would make a good cartoon.

dialogue.text: It's also, I think it's a search in some ways, not only a search for a child, you know, here he is adopting a child as he's writing a book, guaranteed to appeal to children.
dialogue.zh: 我認為這也是一種尋找，不僅是尋找一個孩子，你知道，他在寫書的同時收養了一個孩子，這本書肯定會吸引孩子們。
dialogue.ja: また、これはある意味での探求でもあります。子供を探しているだけでなく、彼は本を書きながら子供を養子にしており、その本は子供たちに確実に受け入れられるものでした。
dialogue.local: It's also, I think it's a search in some ways, not only a search for a child, you know, here he is adopting a child as he's writing a book, guaranteed to appeal to children.
dialogue.en: It's also, I think it's a search in some ways, not only a search for a child, you know, here he is adopting a child as he's writing a book, guaranteed to appeal to children.

dialogue.text: But it's in some ways a search for his own childhood because one of the interesting things about animal farmers, trying to work out the basis of the historical reality of the farm and the people who inhabit it.
dialogue.zh: 但這在某種程度上也是尋找他自己的童年，因為《動物農場》中有趣的一點是試圖找出農場及其居民的歷史現實基礎。
dialogue.ja: しかしこれは彼自身の子供時代を探す試みでもあります。『動物農場』の興味深い点の一つは、農場とそこに住む人々の歴史的現実の基盤を探ろうとしていることです。
dialogue.local: But it's in some ways a search for his own childhood because one of the interesting things about animal farmers, trying to work out the basis of the historical reality of the farm and the people who inhabit it.
dialogue.en: But it's in some ways a search for his own childhood because one of the interesting things about animal farmers, trying to work out the basis of the historical reality of the farm and the people who inhabit it.

dialogue.text: I mean, it's a satire of the Russian Revolution from the mid-teams onward, but the actual world that Farmer Jones and his farm workers and the pigs and boxer and the sheep in habitat is definitely pre-war.
dialogue.zh: 我的意思是，這是對俄國革命中期以後的諷刺，但農場主瓊斯、農場工人、豬、拳師和羊群所生活的實際世界，肯定是戰前的。
dialogue.ja: つまり、これは1930年代中頃以降のロシア革命の風刺ですが、ジョーンズ農場主や農場労働者、豚、ボクサー、羊たちが住む世界は明らかに戦前のものです。
dialogue.local: I mean, it's a satire of the Russian Revolution from the mid-teams onward, but the actual world that Farmer Jones and his farm workers and the pigs and boxer and the sheep in habitat is definitely pre-war.
dialogue.en: I mean, it's a satire of the Russian Revolution from the mid-teams onward, but the actual world that Farmer Jones and his farm workers and the pigs and boxer and the sheep in habitat is definitely pre-war.

dialogue.text: I mean, the farmers is virtually unmechanised. There are very few references to motorised transport.
dialogue.zh: 農場幾乎沒有機械化，幾乎沒有提到機動交通工具。
dialogue.ja: 農場はほとんど機械化されておらず、モーター付きの交通手段についての言及もほとんどありません。
dialogue.local: I mean, the farmers is virtually unmechanised. There are very few references to motorised transport.
dialogue.en: I mean, the farmers is virtually unmechanised. There are very few references to motorised transport.

dialogue.text: Farmer Jones and his wife have a lithograph, a queen Victoria in their front run.
dialogue.zh: 瓊斯農場主和他的妻子在他們的前廊掛著一幅維多利亞女王的石版畫。
dialogue.ja: ジョーンズ農場主とその妻は、前の廊下にヴィクトリア女王のリトグラフを飾っています。
dialogue.local: Farmer Jones and his wife have a lithograph, a queen Victoria in their front run.
dialogue.en: Farmer Jones and his wife have a lithograph, a queen Victoria in their front run.

dialogue.text: As for animal farm itself, the manor farmers, it was originally called, there was a manor farm, not very far from the stores at Mollington where all of them, I lean lived in the late 1930s.
dialogue.zh: 至於《動物農場》本身，原名為莊園農場，位於莫林頓的商店附近，奧威爾一家在1930年代末期住在那裡。
dialogue.ja: 『動物農場』自体は元々『マナーファーム』と呼ばれており、1930年代後半に彼らが住んでいたモリントンの店の近くにありました。
dialogue.local: As for animal farm itself, the manor farmers, it was originally called, there was a manor farm, not very far from the stores at Mollington where all of them, I lean lived in the late 1930s.
dialogue.en: As for animal farm itself, the manor farmers, it was originally called, there was a manor farm, not very far from the stores at Mollington where all of them, I lean lived in the late 1930s.

dialogue.text: There's also a manor farm close, not very far from his parents, home in Southworld.
dialogue.zh: 在南沃爾德他父母家附近也有一個莊園農場。
dialogue.ja: 南ワールドにある彼の両親の家の近くにもマナーファームがあります。
dialogue.local: There's also a manor farm close, not very far from his parents, home in Southworld.
dialogue.en: There's also a manor farm close, not very far from his parents, home in Southworld.

dialogue.text: There's all kinds of ways in which he could have backed that has steepened to his consciousness.
dialogue.zh: 有各種方式讓他能將這些經歷融入他的意識中。
dialogue.ja: 彼がこれらを意識の中に取り込んだ方法はいろいろあります。
dialogue.local: There's all kinds of ways in which he could have backed that has steepened to his consciousness.
dialogue.en: There's all kinds of ways in which he could have backed that has steepened to his consciousness.

dialogue.text: Or it was also quite a small holder when he lived in Mollington.
dialogue.zh: 當他住在莫林頓時，那裡也是一個相當小的農場。
dialogue.ja: 彼がモリントンに住んでいた頃、そこはかなり小さな農場でもありました。
dialogue.local: Or it was also quite a small holder when he lived in Mollington.
dialogue.en: Or it was also quite a small holder when he lived in Mollington.

dialogue.text: And one of the goats that he raised was called Muriel, just like Muriel the goat in animal farm.
dialogue.zh: 他養的一隻山羊叫做穆里爾，就像《動物農場》裡的山羊穆里爾一樣。
dialogue.ja: 彼が飼っていたヤギの一匹はムリエルと呼ばれており、『動物農場』のヤギのムリエルと同じ名前でした。
dialogue.local: And one of the goats that he raised was called Muriel, just like Muriel the goat in animal farm.
dialogue.en: And one of the goats that he raised was called Muriel, just like Muriel the goat in animal farm.

dialogue.text: And interestingly, he didn't like pigs. There are, there's a letter to a friend from Jura where he says, we've been raising a pig here and we don't, the pigs are disgusting animals, and we can't, no one's really going to worry when this one goes to the poor.
dialogue.zh: 有趣的是，他不喜歡豬。他在給一位朋友的信中說，我們在這裡養了一頭豬，我們不喜歡豬，豬是令人厭惡的動物，當這頭豬被送去屠宰時，沒有人會真正擔心。
dialogue.ja: 興味深いことに、彼は豚が好きではありませんでした。ジュラ島の友人への手紙でこう書いています。『ここで豚を飼っているが、豚は嫌な動物だ。この豚が屠殺される時、誰も本当に心配しないだろう』と。
dialogue.local: And interestingly, he didn't like pigs. There are, there's a letter to a friend from Jura where he says, we've been raising a pig here and we don't, the pigs are disgusting animals, and we can't, no one's really going to worry when this one goes to the poor.
dialogue.en: And interestingly, he didn't like pigs. There are, there's a letter to a friend from Jura where he says, we've been raising a pig here and we don't, the pigs are disgusting animals, and we can't, no one's really going to worry when this one goes to the poor.

dialogue.text: On farms over it, it operated by pigs. There is all a...
dialogue.zh: 在農場裡，豬掌控一切。這一切都是……
dialogue.ja: 農場では豚が支配しています。すべてが……
dialogue.local: On farms over it, it operated by pigs. There is all a...
dialogue.en: On farms over it, it operated by pigs. There is all a...

dialogue.text: All as we know, there's an extremely strange person emotionally and the way that he regarded the world.
dialogue.zh: 正如我們所知，他在情感上是一個非常奇怪的人，他看待世界的方式也很特別。
dialogue.ja: ご存知のように、彼は感情的に非常に奇妙な人物であり、世界の見方も独特でした。
dialogue.local: All as we know, there's an extremely strange person emotionally and the way that he regarded the world.
dialogue.en: All as we know, there's an extremely strange person emotionally and the way that he regarded the world.

dialogue.text: And even at the time that animal farmers become a success, we know that he was always already making his preparations to leave London to go live on the remote in a hebrity in Ireland of Jura where he could raise Richard and get on with 1984, his final book.
dialogue.zh: 即使在《動物農場》成功的時候，我們知道他已經開始準備離開倫敦，去愛爾蘭偏遠的朱拉島生活，在那裡他可以撫養理查德，並繼續寫他的最後一本書《一九八四》。
dialogue.ja: 『動物農場』が成功した時点でさえ、彼はすでにロンドンを離れてアイルランドのジュラ島の辺鄙な場所に移り住み、リチャードを育て、『1984年』という最後の本に取り組む準備をしていたことがわかっています。
dialogue.local: And even at the time that animal farmers become a success, we know that he was always already making his preparations to leave London to go live on the remote in a hebrity in Ireland of Jura where he could raise Richard and get on with 1984, his final book.
dialogue.en: And even at the time that animal farmers become a success, we know that he was always already making his preparations to leave London to go live on the remote in a hebrity in Ireland of Jura where he could raise Richard and get on with 1984, his final book.

dialogue.text: After that, he lives on, he lives on Jura. And there is this sense that he's kind of retreating from the world, that the idea of being a public man, a literary celebrity, was really not his taste.
dialogue.zh: 之後，他住在朱拉島。感覺他有點從世界退縮，成為公眾人物、文學名人的想法並不合他的胃口。
dialogue.ja: その後、彼はジュラ島に住み続けました。彼は世界から退くような感覚があり、公の人物や文学的な有名人になることは彼の好みではなかったのです。
dialogue.local: After that, he lives on, he lives on Jura. And there is this sense that he's kind of retreating from the world, that the idea of being a public man, a literary celebrity, was really not his taste.
dialogue.en: After that, he lives on, he lives on Jura. And there is this sense that he's kind of retreating from the world, that the idea of being a public man, a literary celebrity, was really not his taste.

dialogue.text: And he wanted to spend the time that remained in this far away from London, he could just getting on with his work and raising his son.
dialogue.zh: 他想把剩下的時間遠離倫敦，專心工作和撫養兒子。
dialogue.ja: 彼は残りの時間をロンドンから遠く離れて過ごし、仕事と息子の育児に専念したかったのです。
dialogue.local: And he wanted to spend the time that remained in this far away from London, he could just getting on with his work and raising his son.
dialogue.en: And he wanted to spend the time that remained in this far away from London, he could just getting on with his work and raising his son.

dialogue.text: I first read animal farm. I suppose when I was a prep school, and I would have been 11, maybe 12, but that's time across the Evelyn, that was Evelyn Bill, who were beginning to get me introduced the fact that my father really, really was.
dialogue.zh: 我第一次讀《動物農場》，大概是在預備學校時期，那時我11歲，可能12歲。那時是伊夫琳·比爾開始讓我了解我父親的真實情況。
dialogue.ja: 私は初めて『動物農場』を読んだのは、予備校の頃で、11歳か12歳だったと思います。その頃、エヴリン・ビルが私に父の本当の姿を教え始めてくれました。
dialogue.local: I first read animal farm. I suppose when I was a prep school, and I would have been 11, maybe 12, but that's time across the Evelyn, that was Evelyn Bill, who were beginning to get me introduced the fact that my father really, really was.
dialogue.en: I first read animal farm. I suppose when I was a prep school, and I would have been 11, maybe 12, but that's time across the Evelyn, that was Evelyn Bill, who were beginning to get me introduced the fact that my father really, really was.

dialogue.text: And so obviously, really animal farm was was the beginning of reading it all well.
dialogue.zh: 所以很明顯，《動物農場》是我開始認真閱讀他作品的起點。
dialogue.ja: だから明らかに、『動物農場』は私が彼の作品を本格的に読み始めたきっかけでした。
dialogue.local: And so obviously, really animal farm was was the beginning of reading it all well.
dialogue.en: And so obviously, really animal farm was was the beginning of reading it all well.

dialogue.text: What did I think of it? And I thought it was, I loved reading it.
dialogue.zh: 我怎麼看這本書？我很喜歡讀它。
dialogue.ja: それについてどう思ったか？私はそれを読むのが大好きでした。
dialogue.local: What did I think of it? And I thought it was, I loved reading it.
dialogue.en: What did I think of it? And I thought it was, I loved reading it.

dialogue.text: It has two or three different levels. It says everything it has to say, you can't, you can't better it, you can't.
dialogue.zh: 它有兩三個不同的層次，說盡了它要說的一切，你無法超越它。
dialogue.ja: それは二、三の異なるレベルがあり、伝えたいことをすべて語っていて、これ以上良くすることはできません。
dialogue.local: It has two or three different levels. It says everything it has to say, you can't, you can't better it, you can't.
dialogue.en: It has two or three different levels. It says everything it has to say, you can't, you can't better it, you can't.

dialogue.text: To a stretch it out a bit further by putting it on the other side of Santa Cruz would probably ruin it. But it was complete as it is.
dialogue.zh: 如果把故事背景放到聖克魯斯的另一邊，稍微延伸一下，可能會毀了它。但它本身已經很完整了。
dialogue.ja: もしこれをサンタクルーズの向こう側に置いて少し伸ばしたら、おそらく台無しになるでしょう。しかし、今のままで十分完成されています。
dialogue.local: To a stretch it out a bit further by putting it on the other side of Santa Cruz would probably ruin it. But it was complete as it is.
dialogue.en: To a stretch it out a bit further by putting it on the other side of Santa Cruz would probably ruin it. But it was complete as it is.
